standards.name: ENA / SRA submission XML/JSON schema (SRA.submission.xsd and related XSDs)
standards.abstract: This documentation describes programmatic submission formats and manifest file conventions used to submit nucleotide sequence data and associated metadata to the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) / SRA. Research objects include Studies, Samples, Experiments, Runs, Analyses and Projects and the data may be provided as XML or JSON documents (or as accompanying data files such as FASTA, FASTQ, BAM, CRAM, GFF, TAB, etc.). The material is maintained by the ENA (part of EMBL-EBI) and explains the submission endpoints (Webin REST V2, Webin-CLI), the allowed object/document types, manifest file formats (plain text tab-separated or JSON), and permitted file groups for different analysis/assembly types. It addresses problems around consistent programmatic submission, validation, and required file-type groupings and gives concrete field names, example manifests, and allowed file-format lists.

classification.rationale: The source material contains concrete field-level structures and explicit tables/checklists (manifest field names with their meanings and concrete file-type tables for analysis/assembly submissions). These are named fields with concrete formats (e.g. FASTA -> file, STUDY -> accession/alias), therefore the source is best represented as a Metadata Table.

standards.name: ENA Sequence Data Classes (controlled vocabulary)
standards.abstract: This page documents ENA "Sequence" domain data classes: named classes of nucleotide sequence records (e.g., EST, GSS, WGS) that represent specific kinds of sequences or assemblies, with short definitions and an example accession for each. The research objects covered are nucleotide sequence records (targeted sequences, assembled scaffolds/contigs, transcriptome assemblies, etc.), and the page also notes available file formats (EMBL (TEXT) or FASTA). The standard is maintained by the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) and serves as a controlled vocabulary/classification to describe the type of sequence records submitted or held in ENA, addressing the need to distinguish different sequence-record kinds across submission, discovery and retrieval workflows.

classification.rationale: The source presents a concrete tabular listing of named data-class values (Data Class | Definition | Example). This is a controlled vocabulary (enumeration) of sequence data classes rather than prose guidance or an ordered workflow, so it is best represented as a table with a controlled_vocabulary field listing the enumerated values.

sequence_data_class.name: Sequence data class
sequence_data_class.descr: Controlled vocabulary of ENA sequence data classes (named record types) with definitions and example accessions.
sequence_data_class.evidence: The ENA holds different data classes of nucleotide sequence which fall under the three tiers of ENA: reads, assembly and annotation within the Sequence domain.
